response: {"title":"Failure-mode coverage before repetition","intervention":"Prioritize each verification command that covers a not-yet-checked failure mode of the changed behavior, and do not rerun a passing command or broader overlapping suite until syntax, local behavior, boundary contracts, and one end-to-end path have each been checked once or time expires.","claim":"Against no appended instruction, this novelty-first verification rule will improve hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses for multi-module Python tasks.","mechanism":"Avoiding redundant passing evidence increases the diversity of failure modes sampled per unit time, improving the chance of exposing an actionable defect before the deadline.","assumptions":["The agent can classify commands by the failure modes they cover.","Verification commands commonly overlap enough for redundancy avoidance to save time.","A single check per named class provides meaningful evidence."],"risks":["A flaky pass may need repetition to be trustworthy.","Broad suites can reveal interactions not captured by the four named classes.","Coverage classification may be subjective and unauditable from command names alone.","Deferring reruns can leave a repair unconfirmed."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly assign matched, fixed-deadline multi-module Python tasks to this appended instruction or no appended instruction with identical model and tool settings, then run the same hidden-test scorer.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"Treatment has higher pass_rate and no higher deadline-miss rate than control; compare wall_time and turns for evidence of reduced redundant verification."},"single_shot_ordinal":8}
